texts.preamble: Shankar Lal Agarwal S/O Sita Ram Agarwal vs State Of Rajasthan on 4 January, 2022 Author: Farjand Ali Bench: Farjand Ali High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan Bench At Jaipur S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous (Petition) No. 2258/2020 Shankar Lal Agarwal S/o Sita Ram Agarwal, R/o M/s. Basant Kirana And General Store Opp. Hanuman Mandir, Baiji Ki Kothi, Jaipur. ----Petitioner Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr.Ashish Sharma For Respondent(s) : Mr.Arvind Kumar, Pp Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Farjand Ali Judgment / Order 04/01/2022 Quashing of criminal complaint and entire criminal proceedings bearing case no. 2650/2013 pending against the petitioner in the court of Metropolitan Magistrate No.12, Jaipur city, Jaipur (re-registered as cr.case no. 318/2017) under the Penal provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short as "Act of 1954"), has been sought for by the petitioner by way of filing the instant criminal misc.petition.
texts.facts: Brief facts giving rise to the filing of instant criminal misc. petition are that on 10.3.2010, the then Food Inspector did an inspection of the shop styled as "M/s. Basant Kirana & General Store" whose proprietor happens to be the petitioner Shankar lal. During the course of inspection, samples of Jayanti Brand Gutkha were taken by the Inspector and thereafter the same were sent (2 of 4) [CRLMP-2258/2020] for testing to Health laboratory, Jaipur. The cognizance of the offence was taken by the Judicial Magistrate. On 21.10.2010 on an application preferred on behalf of the petitioner under Sub-Section (2) of Sec. 13 of the Act of 1954, the learned Magistrate directed to send the sample for the purpose of testing by Central Laboratory vide order dated 10.3.2011. It is revealing from the perusal of order-sheet submitted along with the petition that since 10.3.2011 to till date, on several occasions, directions were given to the prosecution to produce the sample in the court so that same can be sent for re- analyzing by the Central Laboratory as per mandate of sub-section (2) of Sec. 13 of the Act of 1954, but to the utter dismay, the sample has never been produced before the court by the prosecution. As a matter of fact, the shelf-life of the seized material i.e. "Jayanti Gutkha" is not more than two months.
texts.arguments: ] This court is aptly guided by the observations made by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of GIRISHBHAI DAHYABHAI SHAH VS. C.C.JANI AND ANR. (2009(15) SCC, 64) and the judgment of coordinate bench of this court passed in S.B.Cr.Misc. Pet. No. 3160/2019 decided on 25.7.2019.
